newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran president-elect pressured over cabinet choice.
newsitem.headline: Iran president-elect pressured over cabinet choice.

text.p: Iran's moderate president-elect Mohammad Khatami is being pressured by conservatives over the choice of ministers to his cabinet, Iranian newspapers said on Tuesday.
"Khatami is said to be pressured by various factions which want representation in his cabinet," the daily Iran News said.

Conservative Shi'ite Moslem clerics, whose candidate Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri lost to Khatami by a wide margin in the polls last month, have not minced words in demanding input over the choice of ministers.
"If Khatami...consults with the Majlis before introducing his cabinet, he would not face any problems in winning the Majlis vote of confidence," Tehran deputy Ali Movahedi Savoji told Iran News.
The conservatives have a majority in the Majlis, or parliament, and could block candidates submitted by Khatami who was elected with nearly 70 percent of some 29 million votes.
But Khatami's backers, who include centrists close to outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and left-wing Islamists, said the new president should be allowed to pick a team of his own choice.

"Some organisations and groups have put forth proposals and Mr Khatami has received these proposals, but the final decision will be taken by Mr Khatami alone," Mehdi Karrubi, leader of a clerical group which backs Khatami, told the daily Akhbar.
A student group backing Khatami has urged him to publicise any factional jostling and attempts to influence his choice.

A former culture minister with a reputation as a tolerant politician, Khatami has said he would look beyond factional barriers in picking his cabinet. But he has refused to name any potential candidates.

Newspapers have speculated that his choices might include technocrats such as Central Bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh and Tehran's mayor Gholamhossein Karbaschi and perhaps a woman minister, a first since Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.
The president-elect, who will replace Rafsanjani in August, will also discuss his list with spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei who has supreme power over all state institutions.

Abdollah Nouri, a parliament deputy who was expected earlier this month to run with backing from pro-Khatami deputies for the speakership of the assembly, told newspapers he dropped out of the race after Khamenei told him it was more "expedient" if Nateq-Nouri was re-elected.
Nateq-Nouri, who was humiliated after losing the presidential elections despited backing from most of the clerical establishment, was re-elected as speaker unopposed.
Tehran-based diplomats said Khamenei might demand to name key ministers such as those for foreign affairs, defence, interior and intelligence (internal security).
